F01 Loop and built-in tools

Loop shape

F01.loop-shape How a turn runs: plan, tool call, result, stop.

GitHub Copilot CLI

● supported ! unverified [unverified: no verified evidence record; settles by A tester pass of this supported cell against its cited quotes. It was outside the 30% verification sample.]

Value: The runtime emits a span tree per agent interaction: an invoke_agent root span with chat and execute_tool child spans. Copilot CLI can answer questions, plan work, and complete tasks. By default a plain prompt sent while Copilot is thinking is treated as steering; Ctrl+C acts immediately, canceling the current operation and clearing queued prompts.

Evidence:

  • E-copilot-cli-01163

    The runtime emits a hierarchical span tree for each agent interaction. Each tree contains an `invoke_agent` root span, with `chat` and `execute_tool` child spans.

    Source: https://docs.github.com/api/article/body?pathname=/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-command-reference; retrieved 2026-10-04; version not recorded; tier E1

  • E-copilot-cli-01730

    Copilot CLI is a terminal-based AI agent that can answer questions, plan work, and complete tasks on your behalf. It’s designed to be highly extensible, and there are various ways in which you can customize its behavior and extend its capabilities.

    Source: https://docs.github.com/api/article/body?pathname=/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-cli/comparing-cli-features; retrieved 2026-10-04; version not recorded; tier E1

Value: The agent loop is the repeated reasoning, action and validation steps. When a model requests a tool call, VS Code executes the tool and feeds the result back to the model for the next iteration. Agents self-correct when they encounter errors. A request in progress can be steered, given a queued follow-up, or stopped; stopping does not undo completed actions.

    Source: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/concepts/agents.md; retrieved 2026-10-04; version not recorded; tier E1

  • E-copilot-vscode-00375

    models don't execute code or access files directly. Instead, they generate text that the [agent loop](/docs/agents/concepts/agents.md#agent-loop) interprets as actions. When a model requests a tool call, VS Code executes the tool and feeds the result back to the model for the next iteration.

Turn and step limits

F01.turn-limits Caps on turns, steps or tokens per run, and stop conditions.

GitHub Copilot CLI

◐ partial

Value: --max-autopilot-continues=COUNT sets the maximum number of continuation messages in autopilot mode and must be a non-negative integer; malformed values are rejected. Autopilot pauses when the maximum continuation limit is reached. Example: --autopilot --yolo --max-autopilot-continues 10 with -p restricts it to 10 continuations.

Shell execution tool

F01.shell-tool How commands run: shell, working directory, timeouts, output handling.

GitHub Copilot CLI

● supported ! unverified [unverified: no verified evidence record; settles by A tester pass of this supported cell against its cited quotes. It was outside the 30% verification sample.]

Value: Local sandboxing is off by default; until enabled, shell commands run directly on the machine with the same access as the user's account. copilot --allow-tool='shell' allows Copilot to use any shell command without individual approval. Shell commands are analyzed before execution to identify potentially dangerous patterns.

Evidence:

  • E-copilot-cli-00289

    Local sandboxing is turned off by default. Until you enable it, the shell commands that Copilot runs execute directly on your machine with the same access as your user account: they can read, write, and delete wherever you can, reach any network your machine can reach, and use your credentials

    Source: https://docs.github.com/api/article/body?pathname=/en/copilot/concepts/security-governance-and-network-settings/about-cloud-and-local-sandboxes; retrieved 2026-10-04; version not recorded; tier E1

  • E-copilot-cli-00564

    The tool specification is optional. For example, `copilot --allow-tool='shell'` allows Copilot to use any shell command without individual approval.

    Source: https://docs.github.com/api/article/body?pathname=/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/set-up-copilot-cli/configure-copilot-cli; retrieved 2026-10-04; version not recorded; tier E1

◐ partial

Value: By default, sandboxed commands and tools can write within the current working directory and temporary folders; the home directory, system and tool locations are read-only, and other disk locations are blocked. ◐ partial

Rate-limit behaviour

F22.rate-limits Plan limits, windows and what happens at the limit.

GitHub Copilot CLI

◐ partial

Value: Rate limits control how many requests a user or application can make in a given time period. Included AI credits do not carry over; the allowance resets at 00:00:00 UTC on the first day of each calendar month. Rate limits are temporary; waiting a short period and retrying often resolves them. A setting, when true, switches to auto mode and retries on eligible rate limit errors.

Limitation: The automatic switch to auto mode does not apply to global rate limits or BYOK providers.

GitHub Copilot CLI

Value: Prompt caching is provider and model dependent. When supported, the provider might reuse the beginning of a request that matches cached content; a change early in the request can reduce the reusable prefix. Stable context across turns lets the provider reuse tokens, and forking a session preserves the prompt cache. The Cache Explorer shows cache hit rates.

Limitation: Provider and model dependent: applies only when it is supported, and the provider 'might' reuse the matching prefix. No cache lifetime or on/off setting appears in the quotes.

Tool output limits

F23.tool-output-limits Limits on how much tool output enters the context and how it is cut (truncated, summarized or saved to a file), and any setting that changes them.

GitHub Copilot CLI

● supported

Value: Tool output larger than 20 KiB is saved to a temporary file by default; the model gets the file path and a preview. Applies to all tools, including MCP server tools. Set `COPILOT_LARGE_OUTPUT_THRESHOLD_BYTES` to a positive number of UTF-8 bytes before starting the CLI to change the limit (higher leaves less context).

Evidence:

  • E-copilot-cli-80046

    To prevent a single tool response from consuming too much of the context window, tool output larger than 20 KiB is saved to a temporary file by default. The model receives the file path and a preview instead of the full output. This applies to all tools, including tools provided by MCP servers.

    Source: https://docs.github.com/api/article/body?pathname=/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-cli/context-management; retrieved 2026-10-05; version not recorded; tier E1
